**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My husband does some work in the city now, so I handle most of the fieldwork myself, though my son helps during harvest. I have about 8 mu of contracted land.

Here in southern Hebei, everyone grows winter wheat and summer maize — two crops a year on the same land. That's what I know, that's what the market accepts, and that's what the grain station nearby buys. I'm not going to try cotton or vegetables. My back isn't what it was, and vegetables need too much daily attention.

For wheat I'll use Jimai improved seed — it's what my neighbor uses and she got good yields last year. Not hybrid, just improved. For maize I'll use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, same as always. The seed dealer in town stocks it.

I'll apply compound fertilizer as base before planting wheat, then top-dress with urea when it greens up in spring. For maize I put down compound at planting and urea at the big bell stage. I know I put a bit more fertilizer than some people say I should, but my father did it this way and I don't want to risk a poor harvest.

Irrigation — I'll do three times for wheat: once before winter, once at jointing, once at heading. The water table has dropped but I still have access to the tube well. For maize I usually just do one watering if July is dry; the summer rains normally help.

I'll do rotary tillage for wheat, and for maize I'll just direct-seed into the wheat stubble right after harvest — no time for deep tillage in June.
